before.title: 1.5 dCi (K9K) Turbocharger Failure from Oil Starvation
before.description: The K9K 1.5 dCi diesel in the Mégane II and III suffers well-documented turbocharger failures caused by oil starvation: extended oil-change intervals let carbon sludge block the narrow turbo oil feed pipe and sump pickup strainer, starving the turbo bearings. A sticking EGR valve raising exhaust gas temperatures accelerates the bearing failure. Owners report sudden loss of power, a whining turbo and blue smoke; if debris from the failed turbo enters the engine, the bill escalates sharply.
before.solution: Replace the turbocharger together with new oil feed and return pipes, drop the sump to clean the oil pickup strainer, and perform an oil and filter flush — fitting only the turbo guarantees a repeat failure. Stick to shortened oil-change intervals (10,000 km or less) with the correct low-ash C3 oil.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / limp mode, top speed limited to around 60 mph
Whining or siren noise from the turbo
Blue smoke from the exhaust
Excessive oil consumption or oil smell near the turbo
Underboost fault codes logged

before.title: EDC Dual-Clutch Gearbox Judder, Clutch Pack Wear and Mechatronic/TCU Failure (Mégane III/IV)
before.description: The Getrag-built EDC six- and seven-speed dual-clutch automatics fitted to the Mégane III and IV develop low-speed judder when pulling away, jerky shifts, overheating warnings in stop-start traffic and delayed or clunky reverse engagement. Root causes are dry-clutch friction-pack wear (often by 50,000-75,000 miles), mechatronic valve-block restrictions and TCU software/hardware faults — dealers have acknowledged faulty double clutches as a known problem, and some failures cause complete loss of drive.
before.solution: Mild judder is sometimes cured by a TCM/TCU reprogram and adaptation reset; worn clutch packs need replacement (roughly $1,000-2,000), and mechatronic or TCU failures require unit repair or replacement at $1,500-3,000. Keep to Renault's fluid-change and software-update schedule.
symptoms: Shudder or judder when pulling away from rest
Jerky, abrupt low-gear shifts in city driving
Gearbox overheating warning in stop-start traffic
Delay or clunk when selecting reverse
'Check gearbox' warning, sometimes with loss of drive

before.title: Fuel Supply Hose Leak — Official UK Recall R/2020/189 (Mégane IV)
before.description: Mégane IV cars built between 1 September 2018 and 31 May 2019 were recalled in June 2020 (UK recall R/2020/189) because internal degradation ('internal aggression') of the fuel supply hose can cause a fuel leak. Leaking fuel can reach hot exhaust components, creating a fire risk, and can spill onto the road endangering following traffic.
before.solution: Renault dealers replace the fuel supply pipe free of charge under the recall. Owners of 2018-2019 build cars should check their VIN against the DVSA/Renault recall database and have the work done immediately if outstanding.
symptoms: Smell of petrol/diesel around the engine bay
Visible fuel staining or dripping under the car
Often no symptoms at all before the hose fails — VIN check required

before.title: Keycard 'Card Not Detected' and UCH Body Control Module Failures (Mégane II)
before.description: The Mégane II's keycard ignition system and UCH (Unité Centrale Habitacle) body control module are notorious failure points. The transponder coil inside the keycard breaks loose or the dashboard card reader's contacts wear out, while the UCH itself develops internal relay and solder-joint faults. The result is intermittent or total failure to start, plus cascading electrical gremlins because the UCH controls the immobiliser, central locking, wipers, indicators and lights.
before.solution: Replace or repair the keycard (re-solder the transponder coil) and clean or replace the card reader; persistent multi-system faults need the UCH repaired by a specialist (around $65-150 mail-order) or replaced and recoded. Used UCH units must be programmed to the car.
symptoms: 'Card not detected' message when inserting keycard
Intermittent no-start, then starts after reinserting card
Wipers or lights operating on their own
Central locking or boot release stops working
Dashboard warning lights flickering with relay clicking from UCH

before.title: Rear Caliper Handbrake Mechanism Seizure — Handbrake Won't Hold or Binds (Mégane II)
before.description: On the Mégane II the handbrake actuating lever and mechanism inside the rear brake calipers corrodes and seizes — owners and forum mechanics blame the galvanic coating on the lever and water ingress into the cables and piston gaiters. The mechanism either sticks applied (rear brakes binding and overheating) or fails to return/apply properly, so the handbrake won't hold the car on a hill. It is a recurring UK MOT failure point and creates a roll-away risk when parking.
before.solution: Free off and lubricate the caliper handbrake mechanism and sliders if caught early; most lasting fixes require new rear handbrake cables and replacement (or refurbished) rear calipers, followed by cable adjustment.
symptoms: Handbrake lever pulls high but car still rolls on a hill
Rear brakes binding or stuck on after parking
Hot, smelling rear wheel after driving
MOT failure for handbrake efficiency or imbalance
Grinding or dragging noise from the rear

before.title: K9K 1.5 dCi Timing Belt Failure from Misaligned Fuel Pump Pulley
before.description: Renault's K9K 1.5 dCi diesel engine is prone to premature timing belt failure caused by a misaligned high-pressure fuel pump pulley. The pulley's offset rubs the back of the belt, shredding it; when it breaks, the interference engine destroys valves and pistons. Renault revised the pulley design under TSB 04-040 and similar campaigns. Replacement belt + pulley kit runs €400-800 in parts; engine replacement after a snap costs €4,000-8,000.
before.solution: Replace the timing belt kit at reduced intervals (every 60,000 miles). Inspect and replace the front crankshaft seal to prevent oil contamination. Include the water pump in the replacement.
symptoms: Belt squeal
Oil on timing belt
Rough idle
Engine warning light
